title: Playing in the center of the mouth
summary: Metoyer insisted on playing from the center of the lips and breathing from the stomach to build even muscle.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Lips, teeth and breath: the physical craft of brass playing

blocks.x: Do most trumpet players play with their lips wet? I never think about that, Arden. I never played drumming to start with.
I think the majority of them do. I mean, it looks like it comes natural to them. It just comes natural to them.
So they got some of them all in there. What about the mouthpiece? Did he say anything about any special kind of mouthpiece?
Well, no, he didn't. He let me choose whatever he figured would fit my armature better, you know. He was very particular of me trying to play in the center of my mouth.

In the center. If I could build a muscle up in the center, you see, that would keep too much air pressure from coming out on each side. See, if you're too much to one side, this side gets weak. You're not strengthening this side because you're not planting in the middle. See, eventually air going to come out of here and you're going to puff out on this side or you're going to puff out. But direct in the center, you breathe down in your stomach. You don't breathe from the side of your mouth.
